data.title: santec Holdings' (TSE:6777) Earnings Are Weaker Than They Seem
data.description:
santec Holdings Corporation's (TSE:6777) stock was strong after they recently reported robust earnings. However, we think that shareholders may be missing some concerning details in the numbers.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Zooming In On santec Holdings' Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

santec Holdings has an accrual ratio of 0.27 for the year to September 2026. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, which is hardly a good thing. In fact, it had free cash flow of JP¥6.4b in the last year, which was a lot less than its statutory profit of JP¥10.7b. At this point we should mention that santec Holdings did manage to increase its free cash flow in the last twelve months

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On santec Holdings' Profit Performance

santec Holdings didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. Therefore, it seems possible to us that santec Holdings' true underlying earnings power is actually less than its statutory profit. But on the bright side, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last three years. At the end of the day, it's essential to consider more than just the factors above, if you want to understand the company properly. If you want to do dive deeper into santec Holdings, you'd also look into what risks it is currently facing. data.title: Impressive Earnings May Not Tell The Whole Story For Miwon Chemicals (KRX:134380)
data.description:
Unsurprisingly, Miwon Chemicals Co., Ltd.'s (KRX:134380) stock price was strong on the back of its healthy earnings report. However, our analysis suggests that shareholders may be missing some factors that indicate the earnings result was not as good as it looked.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Miwon Chemicals' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Miwon Chemicals recorded an accrual ratio of 0.27. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit. To wit, it produced free cash flow of ₩19b during the period, falling well short of its reported profit of ₩48.2b. Miwon Chemicals shareholders will no doubt be hoping that its free cash flow bounces back next year, since it was down over the last twelve months.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Miwon Chemicals.

Our Take On Miwon Chemicals' Profit Performance

Miwon Chemicals didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. Because of this, we think that it may be that Miwon Chemicals' statutory profits are better than its underlying earnings power. But on the bright side, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last three years. The goal of this article has been to assess how well we can rely on the statutory earnings to reflect the company's potential, but there is plenty more to consider. data.title: Satellite Approvals Might Change The Case For Investing In Globalstar Stock (GSAT)
data.description:
• Globalstar secured long term French government approvals for its third generation C 3 mobile satellite system, covering Big LEO spectrum usage, launch, and operation of a 48 satellite LEO constellation plus in orbit spares supported by a global ground antenna network.
  • The French and broader multi country authorizations, now spanning more than 20 jurisdictions and over one billion people, materially expand Globalstar's addressable footprint for direct to device services and future IoT connectivity contracts.
  • Attention now shifts to what this wider C 3 regulatory footprint could mean for Globalstar's investment narrative and capital heavy execution.

Globalstar Investment Narrative Recap

To own Globalstar, you need to believe the C 3 constellation, D2D services and IoT modules can turn heavy satellite and ground spend into durable service revenue, not just headlines. The French C 3 approvals widen the regulatory runway, but the immediate operating story still hinges on filling that capacity with paying users.

The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights high capex and deployment timing as key pressure points. Recent quarterly numbers showed revenue at US$70.9 million and a net loss of US$15.68 million, so in the near term the biggest swing factor is whether management can fund the buildout without stretching the balance sheet.

The most relevant recent announcement is the French authorization for Globalstar’s C 3 system across the Big LEO band for 20 years and for the constellation’s 13 year design life. That cements regulatory backing for 48 operational LEO satellites plus in orbit spares and 89 ground antennas, which directly underpins the C 3 rollout described in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St.

For you as an investor, this matters because many of the cited catalysts, from government connectivity contracts to higher IoT usage, rely on that C 3 capacity actually being available and compliant. The approval does not reduce capex intensity or execution risk by itself, but it removes an important regulatory doubt and shifts attention back to launch timing, commercialization and cash burn.

Globalstar Forecasts and What Needs To Go Right

Globalstar's narrative projects US$469.8 million in revenue and US$136.4 million in earnings by 2029. This is based on an assumption of 19.2% yearly revenue growth and a projected earnings swing of about US$215.7 million from a current earnings loss of US$79.3 million.

data.title: What Altria Group Shareholders Got Right
data.description:
If you only glanced at headlines about cigarette declines and regulatory probes, Altria Group might have looked like a stock to avoid. For Altria Group shareholders, the return over the past year was 43.9%, including dividends. That is a striking outcome for a business facing falling volumes, FDA scrutiny and competition from smoke free rivals. If you had been weighing those risks back in November 2025, what information really mattered?

If the move has made Altria Group harder to judge, start where the gap is still open and scan 32 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Two Altria Group Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$58.05 at the start of the period, and the debate around Altria Group was about which story on earnings and regulation would prove closer to reality.

The bullish narrative saw a Fair Value of US$62.88. This was a price implied by assumptions such as a future P/E of 13.8x and a profit margin of 45.2%, supported by confidence in tobacco profitability and dividends.

The cautious view pointed to a Fair Value of US$49.58. This was based on concerns that illicit e vapor, regulatory hurdles, and cigarette declines could pressure margins and smoke free goals.

What The Results Changed For The Altria Group Debate

The clearest new fact was Altria Group lifting Q3 revenue from US$5,251m in 2025 to US$5,441m in 2026, while net income also rose, taking net margin from 45.1% to 46.2%. That outcome leaned toward the bullish story that assumed resilient profitability. Investigations into disclosures around on! PLUS and lowered 2026 guidance pulled the other way. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The single assumption that really got tested was earnings durability. For a different stock, check whether revenue, absolute profit and margin are all moving in the direction the original thesis required, not just one of them.

What Altria Group’s Price Already Assumes

Today Altria Group changes hands at US$77.92. The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St puts its Fair Value below that level, based on a view that the current quote builds in generous assumptions about earnings resilience.

That storyline leans on concerns that smoke free profits and legal risks could strain the business that funds those expectations. Anyone paying today’s price is effectively betting that high margin combustibles and on! earnings can keep supporting that outlook despite those pressures.

"The current numbers imply a share price that treats Altria Group as if resilient EPS guidance, high smokeable margins and large cash returns to shareholders can continue without material disruption from regulatory actions, litigation or mix shifts inside the smoke-free portfolio."

The price and this Narrative do not agree. → Uncover what this Narrative says Altria Group is actually worth

Beyond Altria Group’s Cigarettes

Watching Altria Group means watching one type of long-lived cash flow, based on products facing rising regulatory questions.

One step away, a very different business also leans on long contracts, centered on complex infrastructure and nuclear projects.

The work moves slowly, remains highly specialized and follows client spending plans rather than consumer demand swings.

Execution quality, not shipment volumes, determines how and when value appears.

Your question narrows and deepens together: how should tobacco cash flows sit alongside nuclear and infrastructure projects still unfolding?

data.title: Kaneka (TSE:4118), Why Is Fresh Attention Building Now?
data.description:
Kaneka board meeting puts fresh focus on earnings and dividends

Kaneka (TSE:4118) drew attention on 11 November 2026 after its board met to consider revisions to the consolidated earnings forecast and dividend outlook for the year ending 31 March 2027, a decision point closely watched by shareholders.

That boardroom decision comes after a powerful run in Kaneka’s shares. The stock is at ¥6,533 with a year-to-date share price return of 47.21%, while the 1-year total shareholder return of 59.94% and 5-year total shareholder return of 90.97% point to momentum that investors are now reassessing in light of the revised earnings and dividend outlook.

Scan how Kaneka’s latest forecast rethink compares with other material stocks that are under fresh earnings pressure by reviewing our curated list of list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (24 results).

Kaneka appears to be a solid chemicals and materials platform, and the recent share price surge underlines that reputation. After this run and the revised forecasts, is that strength already fully reflected in the valuation?

Price-to-Earnings of 11.4x: Is it justified for Kaneka?

Kaneka trades on a P/E of 11.4x. With the last close at ¥6,533, that earnings multiple points to a valuation that looks restrained compared with peers despite the strong recent share price run.

The P/E ratio compares what investors pay for each unit of current earnings. For a diversified chemicals and materials group like Kaneka, which spans PVC, advanced polymers, healthcare products and food ingredients, this benchmark helps you gauge how the market is pricing the existing profit base rather than distant forecasts.

Kaneka has high quality earnings and profits that have grown by 4% per year over the past 5 years, with earnings growth of 32% over the last year and net profit margins at 4% compared with 3.2% previously. Against that backdrop, a P/E of 11.4x that is below both the peer average of 13.6x and the JP Chemicals industry average of 11.6x suggests the market is applying a relatively cautious tag to its earnings, even though the stock has outperformed the JP Chemicals sector and the wider JP market over the past year.

The fair P/E ratio is estimated at 12x, so the current 11.4x level is meaningfully lower than where the valuation could trend if sentiment aligned more closely with that fair value benchmark.
